title: Comeback Credit Calculation — Service Accounts and Repair Orders
content:
## The repeat and the original repair
On a Service Accounts and Repair Orders account, comebacks are reviewed when a repair order is paid: the paid repair order is the repair order of the latest payment received on the account, the repeat labor charge is its latest customer-pay labor charge, and the unit is the vehicle on that charge. The original repair is the latest customer-pay parts replacement recorded on the same unit, and its labor charge is the total of the customer-pay labor charges on the same repair order and concern line as that parts charge. Wherever a record is chosen as the latest of its kind and two such records share that date, the one listed first in the records counts.

Where no payment has been received on the account, or the paid repair order carries no customer-pay labor charge, there is no repeat repair to review and no comeback credit. On every account, an original repair line that carries no customer-pay labor charge is a parts sale rather than a repair the store performed, carries no repair warranty, and no comeback credit is owed against it.

## Inside the store's repair warranty
The repeat falls inside the store's repair warranty when the repeat labor charge's line date is on or before the day the tier's repair warranty months (calendar months) after the original repair's line date (that month's last day where it has no such day) and the repeat repair's odometer is no more than the tier's repair warranty miles beyond the original repair's odometer. The odometers are those recorded at check-in on the repeat labor charge and on the original parts charge.

## The credit
The comeback credit is the credit basis times the covered labor share, rounded half up to the cent; it is owed only for a repeat inside the store's repair warranty and only when the original repair is on another repair order, and otherwise there is no comeback credit. The credit basis is the repeat labor charge. The covered labor share is the tier's comeback labor share.

On a commercial fleet account the credit is assembled in this order: first the credit basis is multiplied by the covered labor share; then every deduction this policy sets out is taken off that amount as a share of itself; then every share this policy sets out is applied to it; then every fee refund this policy sets out is added; and the result is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end. On any other account the credit is the repeat labor charge times the tier's comeback labor share, rounded half up to the cent, owed on the same warranty and repair order terms.

## Worked figures (hypothetical, 100% share, 12-month and 12000-mile warranty)
| Repeat labor charge | Original repair | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| 286.40, on 3 May, at 52100 miles | Parts and labor on another repair order, 20 September of the year before, at 47300 miles | 286.40 |
| 286.40 | The original parts are on the same repair order | none |
| 286.40, on 3 May | Original repair 2 May of the year before | none — after the warranty's last day |
| 286.40 | Original line carries parts but no customer-pay labor | none — a parts sale |
